result.narrative:
Larsen & Toubro is operationally sound on the evidence in front of us. Of the eleven news items recorded, ten are severity 0 and most are positive or neutral — a $1.57 billion AI data centre order win, a rare-earth magnet manufacturing expansion, an analyst target upgrade and several stock gains. On the payment side there is a single open overdue notification under policy TCI-WT-2026-0002, 12 days past due, with only one prior notification on record (resolved 6 days late). The payment review flags the trend as "insufficient_history" and notes all notifications come from a single policy, so cross-policy visibility is limited.

The Watch band at 28.4 is almost entirely news-driven. Payment contributes 7.8 of the score; the single Karnataka blacklisting article contributes 20.6, from a base of 60.0 decaying to 58.76 at 11 days old. The adjudicator agreed with caveats and raised three issues with that item: the article body is identical to its headline, so nothing substantiates the assigned severity 3; it describes a minister asking officials to blacklist L&T rather than an executed measure, yet is categorised as regulatory_action; and it is a state-level matter over specific delayed works, not a national debarment. The adjudicator also noted an internal inconsistency in the payment evidence — the notification records 83,000,000 INR owed while the review under the same ID narrates INR 18M and concludes exposure is well covered.

The recommended action is MAINTAIN. The single limit, LIM-IN02-1 for Orvana Steel under TCI whole-turnover policy TCI-WT-2026-0002, stays at 350,000,000 INR with no change, on the basis that PD of 0.1837 sits within the 0.25 appetite target. Maximum liability does not bind and expected loss is unchanged at 46,292,400 either side of the decision. Given the adjudicator's caveats, the underwriter should treat this as a monitoring posture pending two verifications rather than a settled position: reconcile the 83,000,000 INR owed figure against the 18M in the review, and confirm whether the blacklisting is a request or an executed action.

The buyer would move to Healthy below 20.0, which is 8.4 points away. The fastest route there is the news item being downgraded or shown to be a request rather than a completed measure — it is the only non-zero news item, and without it the score falls to 7.8 and the band changes. Otherwise time does the work slowly: the news half-life is 365 days. Clearing the open overdue would also reduce the payment contribution of 7.8.

judgement.bottom_line: Maintain the 350,000,000 INR limit — PD of 0.1837 is within the 0.25 appetite target and the Watch band is almost entirely driven by one unverified news item. The adjudicator agreed with caveats: the blacklisting article's body is identical to its headline, and the payment evidence shows 83,000,000 INR owed in the notification against 18M in the review, so both should be reconciled before the band is treated as settled.
judgement.payment_note: One open overdue notification at 12 days past due under policy TCI-WT-2026-0002, with only one prior notification (resolved 6 days late) and the trend flagged "insufficient_history", so it reads as neither confirmed deterioration nor a clean record — and the owed figure is inconsistent between the notification (83,000,000 INR) and the review (18M).
judgement.news_note: A single severity 3 item — a Karnataka minister asking officials to blacklist L&T over delayed works, 11 days old — carries 20.6 of the 28.4 score, but its article body is identical to its headline and it describes a request rather than an executed action; the other ten items are all severity 0, including a $1.57 billion order win.
lifts_it: Blacklisting item downgraded or confirmed as a request rather than an executed action — score falls to 7.8 and the buyer moves to Healthy
Score falling 8.4 points to below 20.0, the Healthy threshold
Clearing the open 12 DPD overdue, removing the 7.8 payment contribution
worsens_it: Score rising 21.6 points to 50.0, the High Risk threshold
Days past due reaching 38 on the open notification
Karnataka blacklisting progressing from a ministerial request to an executed debarment, or spreading beyond state level
